sentences.text:
3 11-01-2023 I.A. No. 1 / 2022 The present interlocutory application has been filed for deletion of the name and substitution of the legal heirs of the petitioners nos. 7 (Ram Sagar Singh), 12 (Ram Bachan Yadav),
13 (Laxhman Yadav), 14 (Sahodara Kunwar), 25 (Shivpujan Singh), 36 (Ibrahim Ansari), 44 (Haridwar Singh ), 63 (Muniya Kunwar), 67 (Gangotari Kunwar), 72 (Raja Ram Singh), 80 (Ram Naresh Yadav), 103 (Dwarika Ram), 104 (Suraj Singh) & 105 (Ramadhar Singh) who died on 05.08.2020, 15.06.2020, 02.03.2020, 25.10.2020, 03.05.2021, 01.08.2020, 18.12.2020, 27.11.2019,
23.12.2020, 18.12.2019, 18.12.2019, 17.08.2021, 02.04.2019 & 21.04.2021 respectively during pendency of this Patna High Court CWJC No.12710 of 2019(3) dt.11-01-2023 writ application leaving behind their legal heirs, whose details are mentioned in paragraph nos. I to XIV of the I.A No. 1/2022.
Taking into consideration the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners and the nature of prayer made in the interlocutory application, the same is allowed.

Accordingly, the name of the petitioners nos. 7, 12, 13, 14, 25, 36, 44, 63, 67, 72, 80, 103, 104 & 105 is directed to be expunged from the array of parties and in their place their legal heirs, whose details are mentioned in paragraph nos. - I to XIV of the interlocutory application is substituted.

The contention of the petitioners is that their land has been acquired by the National Highways Authority of India (for short the "N.H.A.I.") but adequate compensation has not been granted to the petitioners inasmuch instead of giving compensa- tion at commercial rate, the petitioners have been given com- pensation only treating their land as agricultural land.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that com- pensation of the subject land acquired by the N.H.A.I. is not adequate and for enhancement of the same the petitioners have filed petition before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Ro- htas, Sasaram.
On the other hand, Mr. S.N. Pathak, learned counsel Patna High Court CWJC No.12710 of 2019(3)
dt.11-01-2023 appearing for the N.H.A.I. submits that as per Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the "N.H. Act") "if the amount determined by the competent au- thority under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by ei- ther of the parties, be determined by the Arbitrator to be ap- pointed by Central Government".
He next submits that now the Central Government has notified Divisional Commissioner of the area as Arbitrator under the N.H. Act.

6 In view of the aforesaid, petitioners are directed to file their claim for enhancement of compensation amount as per Section 3-G(5) of the N.H. Act before the Arbitrator i.e. Divi- sional Commissioner,
Patna within a period of four weeks from today.

If such a claim is filed within the aforesaid time, the learned Arbitrator shall decide the same in accordance with law after giving opportunity of hearing to all concerned and will pass a reasoned order within a reasonable time period.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, this writ application is disposed of.

praful/- (Anil Kumar Sinha, J)

opennyai_summary.facts:
The contention of the petitioners is that their land has been acquired by the National Highways Authority of India (for short the "N.H.A.I.") but adequate compensation has not been granted to the petitioners inasmuch instead of giving compensa- tion at commercial rate, the petitioners have been given com- pensation only treating their land as agricultural land.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that com- pensation of the subject land acquired by the N.H.A.I. is not adequate and for enhancement of the same the petitioners have filed petition before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Ro- htas, Sasaram.
On the other hand, Mr. S.N. Pathak, learned counsel Patna High Court CWJC No.12710 of 2019(3)
dt.11-01-2023 appearing for the N.H.A.I. submits that as per Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the "N.H. Act") "if the amount determined by the competent au- thority under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by ei- ther of the parties, be determined by the Arbitrator to be ap- pointed by Central Government".
He next submits that now the Central Government has notified Divisional Commissioner of the area as Arbitrator under the N.H. Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
6 In view of the aforesaid, petitioners are directed to file their claim for enhancement of compensation amount as per Section 3-G(5) of the N.H. Act before the Arbitrator i.e. Divi- sional Commissioner,
Patna within a period of four weeks from today.
If such a claim is filed within the aforesaid time, the learned Arbitrator shall decide the same in accordance with law after giving opportunity of hearing to all concerned and will pass a reasoned order within a reasonable time period.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, this writ application is disposed of.
